title: The Killer - is this Fincher commenting on late stage capitalism? Perhaps not so convincingly

commenti.body: I like the context this take adds to the VO. The constant self-affirmations, his mantras he falls back on when doing an ugly deed start to  sound like the working class refrain: “if I show up, work hard, and always try my best, good things will happen”. Of course the people capable of providing him with those “good things” scrape him off of their boot as soon as he’s not useful, which is an experience all of us are likely familiar with.

That’s definitely part of it. The killer stakes his life on people being apathetic at their jobs. All his IDs are sitcom characters and nobody ever notices cause why would they? If you’re someone who looks at passports all day you’re just trying to get to the end of your shift cause why care about your job. He relies on cops being so buried in case work that they never even get around him. 

The guys in Paris but eats at McDonald’s cause the nature of his work it’s better to just scarf down a McMuffin quickly for sustenance than to get something more substantial. Which I’m sure every worker can relate to. It fuckin sucks working now

What do you think his commentary on late-stage capitalism is if that's what he's doing here? Simply the ubiquitous nature of it? It both seems to make his job harder and easier at given points, so I'm not sure if that's the avenue he's taking. 

I've seen people talk about how the narration can be seen as Fincher commenting on Hollywood. If that's the case I could see this being simply some very tongue-in-cheek 

  
As an aside, I honestly did not find the cinematography anything special. It was technically fine, but besides the close-ups on Fassbender it added very little to any themes that were going on in the actual film.

The whole point of him eating McDonald’s was more to your first point. There are thousands of them in France that serve millions a weeks, so he would not be memorable and just blend in with the hundreds of other people that worker helped that day.
